title: EIGRP Concepts: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Think of a G P S that already has a backup route ready. It's ready before your road even closes. That's E I G R P.

lines.t: A GPS with a backup route

scenes.heading: GPS with alternate routes
scenes.narration: Your G P S knows the main route, and keeps a few safe alternates in reserve. The main route is called the successor. A safe alternate is a feasible successor. It's only safe if it's guaranteed not to loop back through you. If the main road closes, the G P S switches instantly, without recalculating.

scenes.heading: What to check
scenes.narration: Three show commands cover E I G R P. Neighbours. The topology table. And the routes it installs.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. E I G R P is not link state, it's advanced distance vector. It doesn't use T C P or U D P, it has its own transport. And the successor is the lowest total metric, not the lowest reported distance.

items.right: Its own RTP over IP protocol 88

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. E I G R P keeps a main route and safe backups. A backup is safe if its reported distance beats your feasible distance. Internal routes have distance ninety. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva EIGRP lab.

points.t: A main route plus safe backups
